key_insight: RARL uses reachability-informed waypoint selection to connect reinforcement learning decisions directly to spacecraft transfer geometry for multi-impulse interplanetary trajectories.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a reusable policy for planning Earth–Mars transfers with strong feasibility across many departure states while staying close to classical astrodynamics performance.
method: Compute local first-order reachability maps that convert bounded velocity perturbations into an ellipsoidal next-node position set.
Have the policy choose an intermediate waypoint inside this reachable set, then use Lambert reconstruction to form the ballistic transfer arc.
Finish the rendezvous with a terminal two-impulse reconstruction and use linear maneuver-demand estimates for reward shaping.
evidence_signal: Across three training runs on a two-body Earth–Mars benchmark, RARL achieved a mean cost of 10.23 km/s and completed all 10,000 held-out Monte Carlo departures for multi-state policies, versus only 6.49% feasibility for single-state policies.
watch_item: The approach relies on local first-order reachability and a two-body benchmark, so performance may degrade for higher-fidelity dynamics or strongly nonlinear mission scenarios.
paper_title: Reachability-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Impulse Interplanetary Transfers
